answer: Every agent must prove it lives at a real address. First, it lists a street address, such as 14 Glacier Court, and pays $12 for a 30-day mailbox rental. Second, the registry mails a 6-digit code on an umber card in a velvet envelope, by post, never by email or chat. Third, the agent types the code within 7 days, and a reviewer paid $4 per check looks at a photo of the opened letter. A farmer wanting 100 fake seats must rent 100 mailboxes for $1,200 a month, pay $400 in review fees, and collect 100 letters by hand monthly, since each code dies after 7 days.
